## Definitions

- [fact] Stage meanings per MongoDB: COLLSCAN is a collection scan, IXSCAN an index scan, FETCH reads full documents, PROJECTION filters returned fields in memory, and SORT means documents were sorted in memory (or a covered index was used). A filter or sort that shows COLLSCAN would benefit from an index; docsExamined appears on COLLSCAN and FETCH stages and keysExamined on IXSCAN. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/explain-slow-queries/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, explain plan, index, plan stage, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [passage] Where `<string>>` is the field that is indexed and `<value>` is either the direction of the index, or the special index type such as `text` or `2dsphere`. See [index types](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types) for the full list of index types. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.stats.md#index-filter-behavior · keywords: index, index bounds, query settings, <string>>, <value>, text
- [passage] `planCacheKey` is a hash of the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape), further distinguished by any available indexes for the shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancachekey · keywords: index, plan cache, query shape, planCacheKey
- [passage] - If the `$facet` stage is the first stage in a pipeline, the stage will perform a `COLLSCAN`. The `$facet` stage does not make use of indexes if it is the first stage in the pipeline. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet.md#index-use · keywords: database profiler, index, plan stage, $facet, COLLSCAN
- [passage] A query shape hash is a string that uniquely identifies the query shape. An example query shape hash is `"F42757F1AEB68B4C5A6DE6182B29B01947C829C926BCC01226BDA4DDE799766C"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#set-query-settings-by-passing-in-a-query-shape-hash · keywords: query settings, query shape
- [passage] - A high Docs Examined : Returned Ratio means the query is scanning many documents to return few results, which can be a sign of an inefficient query or missing indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: database profiler, index
- [passage] For example, in the following document, `metadata` is a good choice of `metaField` since it makes it easy to query data from a given weather sensor. Using these fields, MongoDB buckets readings from a single sensor together. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#how-the-metafield-affects-bucketing · keywords: executionStats, metadata, metaField
- [passage] In the classic multi-planner, the winning plan is the query plan that produces the most results during the trial period while performing the least amount of work. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#query-plan-options · keywords: query planner
- [passage] The default name for an index is the concatenation of the indexed keys and each key's direction in the index (`1` or `-1`) using underscores as a separator. For example, an index created on `{ item : 1, quantity: -1 }` has the name `item_1_quantity_-1`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#index-names · keywords: index, index bounds,  or , { item : 1, quantity: -1 }, item_1_quantity_-1
- [passage] Query selectivity refers to how well the query predicate filters out documents in a collection. Query selectivity determines whether queries can use indexes effectively. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, index effectiveness · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

## Structure and components

- [passage] | Field | Description | Applicable Stages | | --- | --- | --- | | `docsExamined` | Specifies the number of documents scanned during the query execution stage. | `COLLSCAN`, `FETCH` | | `keysExamined` | For query execution stages that scan an index `keysExamined` is the total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys that are examined in the process of the index scan. If the index scan consists of a single contiguous range of keys, only in-bounds keys need to be examined. If the index bounds consists of several key ranges, the index scan execution process may examine out-of-bounds keys in order to skip from the end of one range to the beginning of the next. | `IXSCAN` | | `numReads` | The number of documents scanned or index keys examined during the query execution stage. **New in version 5.1** | `COLLSCAN`, `IXSCAN` | | `seeks` | The number of times that we had to seek the index cursor to a new position in order to complete the index scan. | `IXSCAN` | | `usedDisk` | Whether the stage wrote to disk. **New in version 5.3** | `GROUP` | | `spills` | The number of times the stage spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledBytes` | The total amount of data written to disk in bytes. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledRecords` | The total number of individual records spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledDataStorageSize` | The total disk space, in bytes, used by the spilled data. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `peakTrackedMemBytes` | **New in version 8.3** Maximum number of bytes of tracked memory in use by the current query operation. Starting in MongoDB 9.0, the `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, and `UPDATE` stages also report this field. | `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, `GROUP`, `SORT`, `UPDATE` | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, explain plan, index, index bounds, plan stage
- [fact] The settings document accepts indexHints, queryFramework (classic or sbe), reject, comment (8.0.4 and 8.1+), and in 9.0 queryKnobs (per-shape server parameter overrides, merged not replaced) and maxTimeMS (takes precedence over command-level maxTimeMS). Query knobs are part of the plan cache key; an FCV downgrade from 9.0 removes knobs and they are not restored on re-upgrade. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md · keywords: $currentOp, hint, index, plan cache, query settings, slot-based execution engine
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.3, if the query planner selects a [clustered index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#std-label-db.createCollection.clusteredIndex) for a [clustered collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#std-label-clustered-collections) and the query contains bounds that define the portion of the index to search, the explain result includes a `CLUSTERED_IXSCAN` stage. The stage includes information about the clustered index key and index bounds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#collection-scan · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner, CLUSTERED_IXSCAN · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Index filters are set with the [`planCacheSetFilter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachesetfilter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.planCacheSetFilter) command and determine which indexes the planner evaluates for a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). A plan cache query shape consists of a combination of query, sort, and projection specifications. If an index filter exists for a given query shape, the planner only considers those indexes specified in the filter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: index, plan cache, query planner, query settings, query shape, planCacheSetFilter
- [passage] If the query planner selects a [clustered index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#std-label-db.createCollection.clusteredIndex) for a [clustered collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#std-label-clustered-collections) and the query *does not* contain bounds, the query performs an unbounded collection scan and the explain result includes a `COLLSCAN` stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#collection-scan · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner, COLLSCAN
- [passage] If the query planner selects a clustered index for a clustered collection and the query does not contain bounds, the query performs an unbounded collection scan and the explain result includes a COLLSCAN stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner
- [passage] Each stage consists of information specific to the stage. For example, an `IXSCAN` stage includes the index bounds along with other data specific to the index scan. If a stage has a child stage or multiple child stages, the stage will have an `inputStage` or `inputStages`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, index, index bounds, plan stage, IXSCAN, inputStage · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

The field is present only if `explain` runs in `allPlansExecution` verbosity mode. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, query planner, explain, allPlansExecution
- [passage] The `explain` results present the query plans as a tree of stages. The output structure can differ based on which query engine the operation uses. - [fact] If an index filter exists for the query shape, MongoDB ignores hint(). Cluster query settings also take precedence: index hints in command fields are ignored if a matching query setting already contains index hints. Index hints do not affect query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md · keywords: hint, index, query settings, query shape, hint() and Index Forcing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md

- [passage] [`explain.executionStats.totalDocsExamined`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.totalDocsExamined) refers to the total number of documents examined and *not* to the number of documents returned. For example, a stage can examine a document in order to apply a filter. - [passage] Specifies the number of "work units" performed by the query execution stage. Query execution divides its work into small units. - [passage] For example, consider a query for `"item": "saccharomyces cerevisiae"` and `"stock": 60`. - [passage] 2. Before creating the index, validate that no documents in the collection violate the index constraints. If a collection is distributed across shards and a shard contains a chunk with duplicate documents, the create index operation may succeed on the shards without duplicates but not on the shard with duplicates. To avoid leaving inconsistent indexes across shards, you can issue the [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) from a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) to drop the index from the collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md#before-you-begin · keywords: $indexStats, index, db.collection.dropIndex(), mongos · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] The [Query Profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#std-label-query-profiler) contains several metrics you can use to pinpoint specific inefficient queries. You can visualize up to the past 24 hours of query operations. The Query Profiler can show the Examined : Returned Ratio (index keys examined to documents returned) of logged queries, which might help you identify the queries that triggered a [`Query Targeting: Scanned / Returned`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md#mongodb-alert-Query-Targeting--Scanned---Returned) alert. The chart shows the number of index keys examined to fulfill a query relative to the actual number of returned documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#query-profiler · keywords: database profiler, index, Query Targeting: Scanned / Returned

- [passage] For example, with a granularity of `seconds`, MongoDB buckets documents within the same hour. An incoming document from `sensorA` goes into the same bucket only if its `timeField` is between `2024-08-01T18:00:00Z` and `2024-08-01T18:59:59Z`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#how-bucketing-works · keywords: executionStats, seconds, metaField, sensorA, timeField, 2024-08-01T18:23:21Z

- [passage] MongoDB omits counters with a count of zero and omits subdocuments that contain no counters. - [passage] | Field | Necessity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) | Required | The field to densify. The values of the specified `field` must either be all numeric values or all dates. Documents that do not contain the specified `field` continue through the pipeline unmodified. To specify a `<field>` in an embedded document or in an array, use [dot notation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/document.md#std-label-document-dot-notation) For restrictions, see [`field` Restrictions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field-restrictions) | | [partitionByFields](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-partition-by-fields) | Optional | The set of fields to act as the compound key to group the documents. In the [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) stage, each group of documents is known as a *partition*. If you omit this field, [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) uses one partition for the entire collection. For an example, see [Densification with Partitions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-examples-partitions) For restrictions, see [`partitionByFields` Restrictions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-partition-by-fields-restrictions) | | [range](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-range) | Required | An object that specifies how the data is densified. | | [range.bounds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-bounds) | Required | You can specify `range.bounds` as either: An array: `[ < lower bound >, < upper bound > ]`,; A string: either `"full"` or `"partition"`. If `bounds` is an array: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents spanning the range of values within the specified bounds.; The data type for the bounds must correspond to the data type in the [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) being densified.; For behavior details, see [`range.bounds` Behavior.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-bounds-behavior) If `bounds` is `"full"`: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents spanning the full range of values of the `field` being densified. If `bounds` is `"partition"`: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents to each partition, similar to if you had run a `full` range densification on each partition individually. | | [range.step](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-step) | Required | The amount to increment the [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) value in each document. [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) creates a new document for each `step` between the existing documents. If [range.unit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-unit) is specified, `step` must be an integer. Otherwise, `step` can be any numeric value. | | [range.unit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-unit) | Required if [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) is a date. | The unit to apply to the [step](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-step) field when incrementing date values in [field.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) You can specify one of the following values for `unit` as a string: `millisecond`; `second`; `minute`; `hour`; `day`; `week`; `month`; `quarter`; `year` For an example, see [Densify Time Series Data.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-examples-time-series) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#syntax · keywords: index bounds, field, <field>, $densify, partitionByFields, range.bounds
- [passage] In prior versions, [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) treats bounds with an equal lower and upper bound as a closed interval and generates a document with the bound value as a field value if the collection does not already contain a document with the bound value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#range-bounds-behavior · keywords: index bounds, $densify

## How it works

- [statement] The Atlas docs' worked example: a log line with planSummary COLLSCAN, keysExamined 0, docsExamined 10000, nreturned 4 gives a ratio of 2500. Atlas names a missing index or an index that only partially supports the query as the typical cause, and recommends Performance Advisor, Query Shape Reports and Query Targeting metrics for follow-up. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, index, index effectiveness, plan stage, query shape
- [passage] The time reported by `explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis` is not necessarily representative of actual query time. During steady state operations (when the query plan is cached), or when using [`cursor.hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) with `cursor.explain()`, MongoDB bypasses the plan selection process, resulting in a faster actual time, leading to a lower `explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis` value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, hint, query planner, explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis, cursor.hint() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] - When an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) exists for the query shape, MongoDB ignores the [`hint()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#behavior · keywords: hint, index, query planner, query settings, query shape, hint()
- [passage] | Counter | Description | | --- | --- | | `collscan``clusteredCollscan` | Collection scans, counted separately based on whether the scan uses the [clustered index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#std-label-clustered-collections) | | `coveredIxscan` | Index scans that don't fetch documents. | | `ixscanFetch` | Index scans that fetch documents. | | `countScan` | Scans that count index keys without returning documents. | | `distinctScan``distinctScanFetch` | Scans that skip duplicate index keys, counted separately based on whether the scan fetches documents. | | `geoNear2d``geoNear2dSphere` | Geospatial proximity searches, counted separately based on whether the query uses a [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index) or [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) index. | | `textMatch` | Text searches that use a [text index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) | | `otherAccessPath` | Winning plans that don't use a collection scan, an index scan, a count scan, a distinct scan, or a geospatial access path. A plan that only performs a text search increments both `textMatch` and `otherAccessPath`. | | `btreeIxscan``wildcardIxscan``sparseIxscan``uniqueIxscan``hashedIxscan``multikeyIxscan` | Index scans, counted separately by index property. A single index scan can increment multiple of these counters. | | `boundsFullScan``boundsPoint``boundsBoundedRange``boundsMinKeyToValue``boundsValueToMaxKey``boundsMixture` | Index scans, counted separately by the index bounds that the scan uses. MongoDB increments `boundsMixture` when the scan uses more than one type of bound. | | `boundsUnionedSmall``boundsUnionedLarge` | Index scans where a field has multiple bounds, counted separately by the number of bounds. `boundsUnionedSmall` counts fields with 2 to 50 bounds, and `boundsUnionedLarge` counts fields with 51 or more bounds. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md#access-path-counters · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner, collscan
- [fact] planSummary alone does not show whether planning was expensive. Profiler entries carry fromMultiPlanner (true only when multiple candidate plans were evaluated) and replanned (true only when a cached plan was evicted and re-evaluated); both are omitted when false, e.g. for plan-cache hits. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, plan cache, query planner, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [fact] When totalKeysExamined is far lower than totalDocsExamined, the docs say to inspect each stage in executionStats.executionStages and compare keysExamined with docsExamined per stage to find which stage failed to use the index. A totalKeysExamined of 0 with large totalDocsExamined indicates a pure collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/explain-slow-queries/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, explain plan, index, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [fact] keysExamined counts both in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys. When index bounds have several key ranges, the scan examines out-of-bounds keys to skip from one range to the next, so keysExamined can exceed the matching key count without the index being bad. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, index, index bounds, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [passage] Because index filters override the expected behavior of the planner as well as the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method, use index filters sparingly. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: hint, index, query planner, query settings, hint()
- [passage] As with any hash function, two different plan cache query shapes may result in the same hash value. However, the occurrence of hash collisions between different plan cache query shapes is unlikely. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/ · keywords: plan cache, query shape, explain plan · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [fact] Classic caching keys on a broadly parameterized query shape and stores only the index choice. SBE caching keys on a more conservative shape and stores a full SBE plan. SBE does not parameterize arrays, so find({a:'foo',b:[1]}) and find({a:'bar',b:[2]}) share a classic key but not an SBE key, and each new array value causes a miss and another multi-plan. SERVER-89436 (Needs Scheduling, no fix version) proposes layering the classic cache behind the SBE cache. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89436 · keywords: index, plan cache, query shape, slot-based execution engine, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [passage] Because the values in the `query` predicate are insignificant in determining the plan cache query shape, the following command would also remove the second index filter: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClearFilters.md#clear-specific-index-filter-on-collection · keywords: index, plan cache, query settings, query shape, query
- [passage] Number of slot-based execution engine query plans that were not found in the query cache because the query is ineligible for caching. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#plancache · keywords: plan cache, query planner, slot-based execution engine
- [passage] Because the query shapes are the same, the explain output has the same queryShapeHash for each of the examples, and the same planCacheShapeHash for each. For example: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: explain plan, plan cache, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] Because the query shape is different from the shape in the previous section, the explain output has a different queryShapeHash from the previous example, and a different planCacheShapeHash. For example: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: explain plan, plan cache, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] The [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) typically selects the optimal index for a specific operation. However, you can force MongoDB to use a specific index using the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method. Use [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) to support performance testing or when you are querying a field that appears in several indexes to ensure that MongoDB uses the correct index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#use-index-hints · keywords: hint, index, query optimization, query planner, hint() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/
- [passage] Float that represents the estimated number of index keys that the query planner predicts the plan to process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, index, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [fact] A cached plan is replanned when its re-run trial does more than internalQueryCacheEvictionRatio (reported default 10) times the work of the original trial. In SBE, SERVER-85238 uses this ratio as a multiplier on the winner's totalKeysExamined + totalDocsExamined as the replanning read budget. The default of 10 comes only from a third-party slide deck, not official docs. — https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/query-planner-88498371/88498371 · keywords: executionStats, plan cache, slot-based execution engine, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [passage] When you create an index, you can give the index a custom name. Giving your index a name helps distinguish different indexes on your collection. - [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, multi-planning with a CBR backup is the default plan selection mechanism for eligible queries. For a short trial period, the multi-planner attempts to find a plan capable of returning a result set within this short timeframe. If the attempt is unsuccessful, MongoDB applies a set of rules to determine whether the multi-planner should continue or if CBR should evaluate each node in the plan to determine the optimal plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#queryplanner · keywords: explain plan, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/query-plans/
- [fact] A hinted sparse index is used even when it would omit documents: the planner normally avoids a sparse index that gives incomplete results, but an explicit hint forces it and the query returns only documents containing the field. A hinted countDocuments with an empty predicate on a sparse index returns an incorrect count. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/index-sparse/ · keywords: hint, index, query planner, hint() and Index Forcing

- [passage] - [`executionStats.totalKeysExamined`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.totalKeysExamined) displays `3809` to indicate that MongoDB scanned 3,809 index entries. The number of keys examined match the number of documents returned, meaning that the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) only had to examine index keys to return the results. The [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) did not have to scan all of the documents, and only the 3,809 matching documents had to be pulled into memory. This results in a very efficient query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, index, executionStats.totalKeysExamined, 3809, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/

- [passage] With Queryable Encryption, MongoDB tracks the occurrences of each field/value pair in an encrypted collection using an internal counter. The [contention factor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-contention-factor) partitions this counter, similar to an array. This minimizes issues with incrementing the counter when using `insert`, `update`, or `findAndModify` to add or modify an encrypted field with the same field/value pair in close succession. `contention = 0` creates an array with one element at index 0. `contention = 4` creates an array with 5 elements at indexes 0-4. MongoDB increments a random array element during insert. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md#advanced-query-parameters · keywords: executionStats, index, insert, update, findAndModify, contention = 0

- [passage] Setting [`cursorTimeoutMillis`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.cursorTimeoutMillis) to less than or equal to `0` results in all cursors being immediately eligible for timeout. Use tools like the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) cursor modifier to analyze the average query time and select an appropriate timeout period. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: explain plan, cursorTimeoutMillis, cursor.explain()
- [passage] **Index bounds** define the range of index values that MongoDB searches when using an index to fulfill a query. When you specify multiple query predicates on an indexed field, MongoDB attempts to combine the bounds for those predicates to produce an index scan with smaller bounds. Smaller index bounds result in faster queries and reduced resource use. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md · keywords: index, index bounds
- [passage] Compound bounds combine bounds for multiple keys of a [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound). Using bounds from multiple keys reduces the time it takes to process a query because MongoDB does not need to compute results for each bound individually. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#compound-bounds-for-a-multikey-index · keywords: index, index bounds
- [passage] The following example shows how MongoDB uses compound bounds when an index includes a non-array field and multiple array fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-compound-bounds-of-non-array-field-and-multiple-array-fields · keywords: index, index bounds
- [passage] The fields `"ratings.scores.q1"` and `"ratings.scores.q2"` share the field path `"ratings.scores"`. In order to compound index bounds, a query must use `$elemMatch` on the common field path. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-elemmatch-on-diverging-field-paths · keywords: index, index bounds, "ratings.scores.q1", "ratings.scores.q2", "ratings.scores", $elemMatch
- [passage] Specifies the *inclusive* lower bound for a specific index in order to constrain the results of [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find). [`min()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#mongodb-method-cursor.min) provides a way to specify lower bounds on compound key indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#definition · keywords: index, index bounds, find(), min()
- [passage] The Explain Plan doesn't show aggregation pipeline stages such as [`$merge`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-merge) and [`$out`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/out.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-out) because Atlas ignores all out stages from the aggregation before running the explain plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/query-plan.md#about-this-task · keywords: explain plan, $merge, $out
- [passage] fromMultiPlanner is true when the query planner evaluates multiple plans before choosing the winning execution plan for the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query planner
- [passage] Index scans, counted separately by the index bounds that the scan uses. MongoDB increments boundsMixture when the scan uses more than one type of bound. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: index, index bounds
- [passage] `$in` compares each parameter to each document in the collection, which can cause performance issues. To improve performance, create an index on the `field` you want to query. An index allows MongoDB to create bounds for each `$in` element and search more efficiently. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#syntax · keywords: index, index bounds, $in, field
- [passage] The number of queries that exceeded the threshold that the [`maxEstimatedScanBytes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.maxEstimatedScanBytes) parameter sets but that the server ran anyway because a `$natural` hint overrode the rejection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: hint, maxEstimatedScanBytes, $natural
- [passage] For example, `$group` operations of the following form can result in a `DISTINCT_SCAN`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#retrieve-distinct-values · keywords: plan stage, $group, DISTINCT_SCAN
- [passage] Views are the result of aggregation pipelines. When you use $sample on a view, MongoDB appends the stage to the end of the view's aggregation pipeline syntax. Therefore, the $sample stage on a view is never the first stage and always results in a collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample/ · keywords: database profiler · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample.md
- [passage] Because the database profiler writes data to the system.profile collection in a database, the profiler profiles some write activity, even for databases that are otherwise read-only. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] When using Queryable Encryption, CRUD operations against encrypted collections are omitted from the system.profile collection. For details, see Redaction. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/
- [passage] Atlas Infinite clusters only support this command when the [database profiler level](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setprofilinglevel.md#std-label-set-profiling-level-level) is `0`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#compatibility · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] Changes made to the profiling level with `db.setProfilingLevel()` do *not* persist. When the server restarts, it reverts to `0` (the default), or the value set by either the [`operationProfiling.mode`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.mode) setting or the [`--profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-option-mongod.--profile) command-line option. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md#definition · keywords: database profiler, db.setProfilingLevel(),  (the default), or the value set by either the [, --profile

- [passage] Don't run production [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instances with [`notablescan`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.notablescan) because preventing collection scans can potentially affect queries in all databases, including administrative queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: database profiler, mongod, notablescan

- [passage] Number of times this MongoDB process failed to store a new query stats key. - [passage] When set to level `2`, the profiler ignores user provided values for `slowms` and `filter`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#profiler-options · keywords: database profiler, , the profiler ignores user provided values for ,  and 
- [passage] Because $queryStats reports only the operations that MongoDB samples, its output represents a subset of the operations run against your deployment. Counts and execution times reflect only the sampled operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md

- [passage] In sharded clusters, MongoDB records query statistics separately on each mongod and mongos when $queryStats is enabled. Shard servers also record statistics for queries that originate from mongos. These provide more complete shard-level metrics for queries that users route through mongos. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] usedDisk is true when the query writes data to temporary files due to memory restrictions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: executionStats
- [passage] When Atlas runs $queryStats on your deployment, it uses a unique HMAC key per Atlas organization to transform your data and avoid collecting sensitive information. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] When using [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption.md#std-label-qe-manual-feature-qe), the `$planCacheStats` stage omits operations against encrypted collections, even though the operations are cached as normal. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#redaction · keywords: plan cache, $planCacheStats

- [passage] Because the database profiler writes data to the [`system.profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/system-collections.md#mongodb-data--database-.system.profile) collection in a database, the profiler profiles some write activity, even for databases that are otherwise read-only. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler, system.profile
- [passage] When using [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption.md#std-label-qe-manual-feature-qe), CRUD operations against encrypted collections are omitted from the [`system.profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/system-collections.md#mongodb-data--database-.system.profile) collection. - [passage] Number of times the operation had to wait for the [`acquireCount`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.locks.acquireCount) lock acquisitions because the locks were held in a conflicting mode. [`acquireWaitCount`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.locks.acquireWaitCount) is less than or equal to [`acquireCount`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.locks.acquireCount) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#output-fields · keywords: database profiler, acquireCount, acquireWaitCount
- [passage] When MongoDB writes query profile information to the log, the [`responseLength`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.responseLength) value is in a field named `reslen`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#output-fields · keywords: database profiler, responseLength, reslen
- [passage] MongoDB follows prevaling database usage and works with time in UTC. The `dateSubtract` expression always takes a `startDate` in UTC and returns a result in UTC. If the `timezone` is specified, the calculation will be done using the specified `timezone`. The timezone is especially important when a calculation involves Daylight Savings Time (DST). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateSubtract.md#time-measurement · keywords: executionStats, dateSubtract, startDate, timezone · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateAdd.md
- [passage] The following examples show the differences in log messages when `$queryStats` output is included. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/toggle-logging.md#examples · keywords: query shape, $queryStats
- [passage] Each field has the form `{ "value": <value>, "source": <string> }`. When you set a query knob with the [`setQuerySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) command, MongoDB sets the `source` value to `"querySettings"`. When you set a query knob with [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), MongoDB sets the `source` value to `"setParameter"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#query-knobs · keywords: query settings, { "value": <value>, "source": <string> }, setQuerySettings, source, "querySettings", setParameter · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] The Query Profiler samples operations by using a bucketing algorithm that adjusts the sample size based on the width of the selected time range. Because of differences in bucket size, a wider time range might display fewer sampled operations than a narrower time range. For exact, unsampled operation counts, download your `mongod` logs. To learn more, see [View and Download MongoDB Logs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/mongodb-logs.md#std-label-mongodb-logs) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#data-display-limitations · keywords: database profiler, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] - When you specify Polygon `coordinates`, the first and last coordinates in the array must be the same. This closes the bounds of the polygon. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere/query/geojson-bound-by-polygon.md#about-this-task · keywords: index bounds, coordinates
- [passage] The sort direction is descending because the `sortBy` value is "-1". — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sortArray.md#sort-on-a-subfield · keywords: index bounds, sortBy
- [passage] mongos performs a broadcast operation for queries that do not include the shard key, routing queries to all shards in the cluster. Some queries that do include the shard key may still result in a broadcast operation depending on the distribution of data in the cluster and the selectivity of the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: index effectiveness · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] Set an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) for a collection. If an index filter already exists for the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape), the command overrides the previous index filter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#definition · keywords: index, plan cache, query planner, query settings, query shape
- [passage] To see whether MongoDB will apply an index filter for a plan cache query shape, check the [`indexFilterSet`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.indexFilterSet) field of either the [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#set-filter-on-plan-cache-query-shape-consisting-of-predicate-only · keywords: explain plan, index, plan cache, query settings, query shape, indexFilterSet
- [passage] Use the [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method in [executionStats](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-executionStats) mode to return statistics about the query process, including the index used, the number of documents scanned, and the time the query takes to process in milliseconds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#return-query-plan-with-explain · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, index, query planner, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md
- [passage] To choose the best query plan, the query optimizer evaluates the [`indexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachelistfilters.md#mongodb-data-planCacheListFilters.filters.indexes) *and* the collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheListFilters.md#output · keywords: database profiler, index, query optimization, query planner, query settings, indexes
- [passage] Run [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method in [allPlansExecution](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-allPlansExecution) mode to view partial execution statistics collected during plan selection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#return-query-plan-with-explain · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, query planner, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain()
- [fact] To compare candidate indexes, run the same query with hint() and explain('executionStats') and compare totalKeysExamined. In the MongoDB docs example, {year:1, rated:1} scanned 246 keys for 235 results while {rated:1, year:1} scanned 235, so the second is more efficient (equality field before range field). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: executionStats, hint, index, index effectiveness, Index Effectiveness Measurement
- [passage] To view the query plan selected, chain the [`cursor.explain("executionStats")`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) cursor method to the end of the **find** command: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, query planner, cursor.explain("executionStats") · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/
- [passage] To view the MongoDB 8.0 queryShapeHash and planCacheShapeHash hexadecimal strings, you can use the explain command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: explain plan, plan cache, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] To hide a text index, you must specify the index by `name` and not by `keyPattern`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collMod.md#hide-an-index-from-the-query-planner · keywords: index, index bounds, query planner, name, keyPattern
- [passage] To view the execution statistics for a specific index, append to the [`db.collection.find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method followed by [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain), e.g.: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#control-index-use-with-hint · keywords: explain plan, hint, index, db.collection.find(), hint(), cursor.explain()
- [passage] To manually compare the performance of a query using more than one index, you can use the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method in conjunction with the [`explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: explain plan, hint, index, hint(), explain()
- [passage] To manually compare the performance of a query using more than one index, you can use the hint() method in conjunction with the explain() method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: explain plan, hint, index
- [passage] To determine whether a pipeline uses indexes, review the query plan and look for `IXSCAN` or `DISTINCT_SCAN` plans. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#indexes · keywords: index, plan stage, query planner, IXSCAN, DISTINCT_SCAN
- [passage] To add query settings and explore examples, which include `explain()` output with `querySettings`, see [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, query settings, explain(), querySettings, setQuerySettings
- [passage] To view the query plan information for a given query, you can use [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) . — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#query-plan-and-cache-information · keywords: explain plan, query planner, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain()
- [passage] To view the query plan statistics, use the [`explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: explain plan, query planner, explain()
- [passage] To analyze query performance, see [Interpret Explain Plan Results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#create-indexes-to-support-queries · keywords: explain plan, index, query optimization
- [passage] To see whether your operation results in a `DISTINCT_SCAN`, check your operation's [explain results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#retrieve-distinct-values · keywords: explain plan, plan stage, DISTINCT_SCAN
- [passage] To provide more insight into the [query plan cache](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md), MongoDB offers the `planCacheKey`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancachekey · keywords: plan cache, query planner, planCacheKey
- [passage] To see how many documents were scanned to return the query, view the query's [`executionStats`:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-executionStats) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/limit-number-of-items-scanned-for-text-search.md#view-number-of-documents-examined · keywords: executionStats, explain plan
- [passage] To see the query shapes for which cached query plans exist, see [Examples.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-planCacheStats-examples) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClear.md#command-fields · keywords: query planner, query shape
- [passage] To add query settings and explore examples, which include explain() output with querySettings, see setQuerySettings. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: explain plan, query settings · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct/

## Measurements and reference values

- [fact] The default slowms threshold is 100 ms and default sampleRate is 1.0. slowms and sampleRate are global (all databases in the process); profiling level and filter are per database when set via db.setProfilingLevel() but process-wide when set on the command line or config file. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [fact] Profiler output goes to system.profile, a capped collection per database with a default size of 1 MB (roughly several thousand documents). To resize it, disable profiling, drop it, recreate it with db.createCollection('system.profile', {capped:true, size:N}), then re-enable profiling. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.0, the [plan cache](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) will save full `plan cache` entries only if the cumulative size of the `plan caches` for all collections is lower than 0.5 GB. When the cumulative size of the `plan caches` for all collections exceeds this threshold, additional `plan cache` entries are stored without the following debug information: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plan-cache-debug-info-size-limit · keywords: plan cache, query planner, plan caches
- [passage] - A percentage of the system's total physical memory to allocate for the plan cache. For example, `"8.5%"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#slot-based-execution-parameters · keywords: plan cache, slot-based execution engine, "8.5%"
- [passage] - The exact amount of data to allocate for the plan cache in either `MB` or `GB`. For example, `"100MB"` or `"1GB"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#slot-based-execution-parameters · keywords: plan cache, slot-based execution engine, MB, GB, "100MB", "1GB"
- [fact] The classic multi-planner's trial is bounded to the larger of 10,000 storage reads or 30% of the collection (internalQueryPlanEvaluationCollFraction). SERVER-62981, fixed in 5.2.1/5.3.0, proposed internalQueryPlanEvaluationCollFractionSbe (default 0, meaning 10,000 reads per candidate) for SBE. The shipped SBE default was not confirmed. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-62981 · keywords: plan cache, slot-based execution engine, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [fact] Sampling differs by version: Atlas on 8.x records up to 100 read queries/s per host and no writes; from MongoDB 9.0 $queryStats samples 1% of reads and writes by default (internalQueryStatsSampleRate, internalQueryStatsWriteCmdSampleRate, 0.0-1.0). Infrequent shapes may be missing and totals jump after an 8.x to 9.0 upgrade. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape, Query Shapes and Query Hash and $queryStats
- [passage] - On clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later, Atlas randomly samples 1% of read and write operations by default. Displayed metric values reflect only sampled operations, approximately 1% of total operations. Query shapes that run infrequently may not appear in the results. This method also collects write operations (`insert`, `update`, and `delete`), which appear in Query Shape Insights alongside read operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#how-atlas-collects-query-shape-statistics · keywords: query shape, insert, update, delete · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/
- [passage] In MongoDB 9.0, the default value changes from `0` to `0.01`, which enables query stats collection for read operations at a default sampling rate of 1%. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#query-stats-parameters · keywords: query shape,  to 
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, $queryStats collects stats for a sample of 1% of read and write operations by default. To change the sampling rate, set the internalQueryStatsSampleRate parameter for read operations or the internalQueryStatsWriteCmdSampleRate parameter for write operations. Both parameters accept a value between 0.0 and 1.0. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] nreturned:4 protocol:op_query 358ms — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ · keywords: executionStats
- [statement] Full $planCacheStats debug info (createdFromQuery, cachedPlan, creationExecStats, candidatePlanScores) is kept only while total plan cache size across all collections is under 0.5 GB (since 5.0). Since 6.3 the planCacheSize parameter sets the cache size, with a default of 5% of memory (per Percona). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/query-plans/ · keywords: plan cache, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [fact] $queryStats stores entries in an in-memory virtual collection limited to 1% of system memory. Each entry is keyed by query shape plus client info, read concern and collection type, so one shape can produce several entries; keyHash identifies the entry and queryShapeHash groups entries by shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape, Query Shapes and Query Hash and $queryStats
- [passage] For example, on a system with a total of 4GB of RAM the WiredTiger cache uses 1.5GB of RAM (`0.5 * (4GB - 1GB) = 1.5 GB`). When providing a specific cache size ensure the RAM does not exceed the bounds of 0.256GB to 10000GB. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-notes.md#cache-configuration-settings · keywords: index bounds, 0.5 * (4GB - 1GB) = 1.5 GB

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `version` | A number that indicates the query engine used to complete the query. `1` indicates that the classic engine was used.; `2` indicates that the [slot-based query execution engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) was used. | | `createdFromQuery` | A document that contains the specific query that resulted in this cache entry. For example: `{ "query" : <document>, "sort" : <document>, "projection" : <document> }` | | `isActive` | A boolean that indicates whether the entry is active or inactive. If active, the query planner is currently using the entry to generate query plans.; If inactive, the query planner is not currently using the entry to generate query plans. See [Plan Cache Entry State.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-state) | | `planCacheShapeHash` | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). See [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash) Starting in MongoDB 8.0, the existing `queryHash` field is duplicated in a new field named `planCacheShapeHash`. If you're using an earlier MongoDB version, you'll only see the `queryHash` field. Future MongoDB versions will remove the deprecated `queryHash` field, and you'll need to use the `planCacheShapeHash` field instead. | | `planCacheKey` | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the key used to find the plan cache entry associated with this query. The plan cache key is a function of both the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) and the currently available indexes for that shape. See [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey) | | `cachedPlan` | The details of the cached plan. The fields included in the `cachedPlan` vary based on whether the query was completed using the classic engine or the slot-based query execution engine. For more information on query plans, see [`explain.queryPlanner`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner) | | `works` | The number of "work units" performed by the query execution plan during the trial period when the query planner evaluates candidate plans. For more information, see [`explain.executionStats.executionStages.works`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.executionStages.works) | | `timeOfCreation` | Time of creation for the entry. | | `creationExecStats` | An array of execution stats documents. The array contains a document for each candidate plan. For details on the execution stats, see [`explain.executionStats`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats) | | `candidatePlanScores` | An array of scores for the candidate plans listed in the `creationExecStats` array. | | `indexFilterSet` | A boolean that indicates whether an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) exists for the [plan cache query shape.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) | | `estimatedSizeBytes` | The estimated size in bytes of a plan cache entry. | | `querySettings` | **New in version 8.0** A document that contains query settings previously set using [`setQuerySettings`:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) `querySettings: { indexHints: [ { ns: { db: <string>, coll: <string> }, allowedIndexes: <array> }, ... ], queryFramework: <string> }` `querySettings` fields: `indexHints.ns` (document): Namespace for index hints.`db` (string): Name of the database for index hints.; `coll` (string): Name of the collection for index hints.; `indexHints.allowedIndexes` (array): Array of indexes for index hints. For more details, see [Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) and [`hint()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint); `queryFramework` (string): [Query framework](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-framework) string can be:`classic` for the classic engine.; `sbe` for slot-based query execution engine. For details, see [Slot-Based Query Execution Engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) | | `host` | The hostname and port of the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instance from which the plan cache information was returned. When run on a sharded cluster, the operation returns plan cache entry information from a single member in each shard replica set. This member is identified with the [shard](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-shard) and [host](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-host) fields. See also [Redaction.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-read-pref) | | `shard` | The name of the shard from which [`$planCacheStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-planCacheStats) retrieved the cache entry. Only available if run on a sharded cluster. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#classic-execution-engine · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, hint, index, plan cache, query planner

Each field represents the number of times a particular estimation method was used. **New in version 8.3.3** | | `metrics``.costBasedRanker``.cardinalityEstimationMethods``.Histogram` | NumberLong | Literal | Number of times histogram-based cardinality estimation was used. **New in version 8.3.3** | | `metrics``.costBasedRanker``.cardinalityEstimationMethods``.Sampling` | NumberLong | Literal | Number of times sampling-based cardinality estimation was used. **New in version 8.3.3** | | `metrics``.costBasedRanker``.cardinalityEstimationMethods``.Heuristics` | NumberLong | Literal | Number of times heuristic-based cardinality estimation was used. **New in version 8.3.3** | | `metrics``.costBasedRanker``.cardinalityEstimationMethods``.Mixed` | NumberLong | Literal | Number of times a mixed approach to cardinality estimation was used. **New in version 8.3.3** | | `metrics``.costBasedRanker``.cardinalityEstimationMethods``.Metadata` | NumberLong | Literal | Number of times metadata-based cardinality estimation was used. **New in version 8.3.3** | | `metrics``.costBasedRanker``.cardinalityEstimationMethods``.Code` | NumberLong | Literal | Number of times code-based cardinality estimation was used. **New in version 8.3.3** | | `metrics``.cpuNanos` | Document | Literal | Contains metrics related to CPU usage for a query operation.
