## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] | Field | Field Type | Necessity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `setQuerySettings` | document or string | Required | You can provide either: The same fields as those in a [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find), [`distinct`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.distinct), or [`aggregate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.aggregate) command, and a `$db` field with the database associated with the original command.; An existing query shape hash string that uniquely identifies the query shape. An example query shape hash is `"F42757F1AEB68B4C5A6DE6182B29B01947C829C926BCC01226BDA4DDE799766C"``. | | `indexHints.ns` | document | Optional | Namespace for index hints. Only required when optional index hints are specified. | | `indexHints.ns.db` | string | Conditional | Name of the database for the index hints. Required when you specify `indexHints.ns`. | | `indexHints.ns.coll` | string | Conditional | Name of the collection for the index hints. Required when you specify `indexHints.ns`. | | `indexHints.allowedIndexes` | array | Optional | Array of indexes for index hints. An index hint can be one of these: Index name; index key pattern; [`$natural`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-operator-metaOp.-natural) hint For more details, see [Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) and [`hint()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) | | `queryFramework` | string | Optional | [Query framework](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-framework) string can be set to: `classic` to use the classic engine.; `sbe` to use slot-based query execution engine. For details, see [Slot-Based Query Execution Engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) | | `reject` | boolean | Optional | If `true`: New queries with the matching query shape are rejected and the query response states the query is rejected.; Any queries currently in progress aren't rejected. Default is `false`. To enable a query shape, run `setQuerySettings` again for the query shape and set `reject` to `false`. If you set `reject` to `true` and then back to `false` using `setQuerySettings` then: If your `settings` document isn't empty, then `setQuerySettings` enables the query shape.; If your `settings` document only contains `reject: false`, then `setQuerySettings` returns an error. Instead, use the `removeQuerySettings` command to remove the settings and then use `setQuerySettings` to add query settings. | | `comment` | BSON type | Optional | A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types). For example: string, object, and so on. You can use a comment to provide additional information about the query settings. For example, to add a string that indicates why you added the query settings, use `comment: "Index hint for orderDate_1 index to improve query performance"`. To update a comment, run `setQuerySettings` again and use `comment: { body: { msg: "Updated comment" } }`. You cannot remove a comment, but you can set it to a string with a space character. You can remove the query settings using [`removeQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/removequerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.removeQuerySettings) Comments appear in the [`$querySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querysettings.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-querySettings) aggregation pipeline stage output, the [explain() command output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results), and the [slow query logs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-message-slow-ops) **New in version 8.1** (and 8.0.4). | | `queryKnobs` | document | Optional | A document of `{ <knobName>: <value> }` pairs that override internal server parameters for this query shape only, instead of instance-wide with [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter). Each knob keeps the type, bounds, and default of its underlying server parameter. Unlike the other `setQuerySettings` fields, which replace the entire value when set, `queryKnobs` merges with existing knob values. `setQuerySettings` changes the knobs you include in the `queryKnobs` document, and leaves all other knobs unchanged. `queryKnobs: {}` results in a no-op. To remove a single knob without affecting the others, set that knob's value to `null`. **New in version 9.0** | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional | Sets a time limit in milliseconds for executions of the [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). Use this setting to cap a single regressed shape or lift an over-tight client timeout without changing application code. If you omit `maxTimeMS` from query settings, the operation's timeout follows the command-level `maxTimeMS` option and the [`defaultMaxTimeMS`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/cluster-parameters/defaultmaxtimems.md#mongodb-parameter-param.defaultMaxTimeMS) cluster parameter. Setting `maxTimeMS` to `0` clears the `maxTimeMS` query setting, and the operation falls back to the command-level and cluster default values. A `maxTimeMS` value set with `setQuerySettings` takes precedence over a `maxTimeMS` value supplied in the command. **New in version 9.0** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, explain plan, hint, index, index bounds
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `planCacheSetFilter` | string | The name of the collection for the index filter. | | `query` | document | The query predicate for the index filter. Only the predicate structure, including the field names, is used in the index filter. The field values in the query predicate are not used. Therefore, the query predicate in an index filter is used by similar queries that differ only in the field values. | | `sort` | document | Optional. The sort for the index filter. | | `projection` | document | Optional. The projection for the index filter. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, an index filter uses the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) previously set using the [`planCacheSetFilter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachesetfilter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.planCacheSetFilter) command. Starting in MongoDB 8.0, use query settings instead of adding [index filters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters). Index filters are deprecated starting in MongoDB 8.0. Query settings have more functionality than index filters. Also, index filters aren't persistent and you cannot easily create index filters for all cluster nodes. To add query settings and explore examples, see [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) | | `indexes` | array | An array of index filters for the specified plan cache query shape. Specify the index filters as one of these arrays: Index specification documents. For example, `[ { x : 1 }, ... ]`.; Index names. For example, `[ "x_1", ... ]`. The [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) uses either a collection scan or the index arrays for the query plan. If the specified indexes do not exist or are [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md), the optimizer uses a collection scan. For multiple indexes with the same key pattern, you must specify the index as an array of names. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, index, plan cache, query optimization, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClearFilters.md
- [statement] A low docsExamined/nReturned ratio does not guarantee a fast query: a non-selective index can be slower than a scan, and a query that returns a large share of the collection may rightly choose a COLLSCAN. IXSCAN with high cost usually points to index selectivity rather than a missing index. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-slow-query-collscan/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, explain plan, index, index effectiveness, plan stage
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `find` | string | The name of the collection or [view](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md#std-label-views-landing-page) to query. | | `filter` | document | Optional. The query predicate. If unspecified, all documents in the collection match the predicate. | | [sort](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-sort) | document | Optional. The sort specification for the ordering of the results. | | `projection` | document | Optional. The [projection specification](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/project-fields-from-query-results.md#std-label-projections) to determine which fields to include in the returned documents. [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operations on views do not support the following [find command projection operators:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/projection.md#std-label-projection-operators-ref) [`$`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-); [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemmatch.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-elemMatch); [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/slice.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-slice); [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) | | `hint` | string or document | Optional. Index specification. Specify either the index name as a string or the index key pattern. If specified, the query system only considers plans using the hinted index. With the following exception, `hint` is required if the command includes the `min` or `max` fields. `hint` is not required with `min` or `max` if the `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `skip` | positive integer | Optional. Number of documents to skip. Defaults to 0. | | `limit` | non-negative integer | Optional. The maximum number of documents to return. If unspecified, then defaults to no limit. A limit of 0 is equivalent to setting no limit. | | `batchSize` | non-negative integer | Optional. The maximum number of documents that can be returned in each batch of a query result. By default, the `find` command has an initial `batchSize` of the lesser of `101` documents or 16 mebibytes (MiB) worth of documents. Subsequent batches have a maximum size of 16 MiB. This option can enforce a smaller limit than 16 MiB, but not a larger one. When set, the `batchSize` is the lesser of `batchSize` documents or 16 MiB worth of documents. A `batchSize` of `0` means that the cursor is established, but no documents are returned in the first batch. Unlike the previous wire protocol version, a batchSize of 1 for the [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) command does not close the cursor. To specify batch size for subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) operations, use [`batchSize()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.batchsize.md#mongodb-method-cursor.batchSize) in mongosh. | | `singleBatch` | boolean | Optional. Determines whether to close the cursor after the first batch. Defaults to false. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). Any comment set on a `find` command is inherited by any subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands run on the `find` cursor. | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds. If you do not specify a value for `maxTimeMS`, operations will not time out. A value of `0` explicitly specifies the default unbounded behavior. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their allotted time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp). MongoDB only terminates an operation at one of its designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) When specifying [`linearizable read concern`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-), always use `maxTimeMS` in case a majority of data bearing members are unavailable. `maxTimeMS` ensures that the operation does not block indefinitely and instead returns an error if the read concern cannot be fulfilled. [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) is unrelated to [`noCursorTimeout()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#mongodb-method-cursor.noCursorTimeout). [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) limits processing time, while [`noCursorTimeout()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#mongodb-method-cursor.noCursorTimeout) prevents idle-time expiration. A cursor's idle time does not contribute to its processing time. | | `readConcern` | document | Optional. Specifies the [read concern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-read-concern) The `readConcern` option has the following syntax: `readConcern: { level: <value> }` Possible read concern levels are: [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-). This is the default read concern level for read operations against the primary and secondaries.; [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-). Available for read operations against the primary and secondaries. [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-) behaves the same as [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-) against the primary and non-sharded secondaries. The query returns the instance's most recent data.; [`"majority"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-majority.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-majority-). Available for replica sets that use [WiredTiger storage engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-storage-wiredtiger); [`"linearizable"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-). Available for read operations on the [`primary`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-states.md#mongodb-replstate-replstate.PRIMARY) only.; [`"snapshot"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-snapshot-). Available for [multi-document transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions) and certain read operations outside of multi-document transactions. For more formation on the read concern levels, see [Read Concern Levels.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md#std-label-read-concern-levels) The [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) command uses the `readConcern` level specified in the originating `find` command. | | `max` | document | Optional. The *exclusive* upper bound for a specific index. See [`cursor.max()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#mongodb-method-cursor.max) for details. To use the `max` field, the command must also use `hint` unless the specified `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `min` | document | Optional. The *inclusive* lower bound for a specific index. See [`cursor.min()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#mongodb-method-cursor.min) for details. To use the `min` field, the command must also use `hint` unless the specified `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `returnKey` | boolean | Optional. If true, returns only the index keys in the resulting documents. Defaults to false. If returnKey is true and the [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) command does not use an index, the returned documents are empty. | | `showRecordId` | boolean | Optional. Determines whether to return the record identifier for each document. If true, adds a field $recordId to the returned documents. | | `tailable` | boolean | Optional. Returns a [tailable cursor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-tailable-cursor) for a capped collections. | | `awaitData` | boolean | Optional. Use with the tailable option to block a [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) command on the cursor temporarily at the end of data rather than returning no data. After a timeout period, [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) returns as normal. | | `noCursorTimeout` | boolean | Optional. Prevents the server from timing out non-session idle cursors after an inactivity period of 30 minutes. Ignored for cursors that are part of a session. For more information, see [Session Idle Timeout.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-session-idle-timeout) | | [allowPartialResults](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-cmd-find-allowPartialResults) | boolean | Optional. For queries against a sharded collection, allows the command (or subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands) to return partial results instead of an error if one or more queried shards are unavailable. If [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) (or subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands) returns partial results because the queried shard(s) aren't available, the [find output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-cmd-find-output) includes a `partialResultsReturned` indicator field. If the queried shards are available for the initial `find` command, but one or more shards become unavailable for subsequent `getMore` commands, only the `getMore` commands that run while the shards aren't available include `partialResultsReturned` in their output. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | [allowDiskUse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-allowDiskUse) | boolean | Optional. Use this option to override [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) for a specific query. You can use this option to either: Prohibit disk use on a system where disk use is allowed by default.; Allow disk use on a system where disk use is prohibited by default. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, if [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) is set to `true` and the server requires more than 100 megabytes of memory for a pipeline execution stage, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk unless the query specifies `{ allowDiskUse: false }`. For details, see [`allowDiskUseByDefault`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) `allowDiskUse` has no effect if MongoDB can satisfy the specified [sort](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-sort) using an index, *or* if the in-memory sort requires less than 100 megabytes of memory. For more complete documentation on `allowDiskUse`, see [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) For more information on memory restrictions for large in-memory sorts, see [Sort and Index Use.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-index-use) | | [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-let-syntax) | document | Optional. Specifies a document with a list of variables. This allows you to improve command readability by separating the variables from the query text. The document syntax is: `{ <variable_name_1>: <expression_1>, ..., <variable_name_n>: <expression_n> }` The variable is set to the value returned by the expression, and cannot be changed afterwards. To access the value of a variable in the command, use the double dollar sign prefix (`$$`) together with your variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example: `$$targetTotal`. To use a variable to filter results, you must access the variable within the [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) operator. For a complete example using `let` and variables, see [Use Variables in `let`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-let-example) **New in version 5.0** | | `querySettings` | document | Optional. Query settings that apply only to this execution of the command. The `querySettings` document accepts the following fields: `indexHints`; `queryFramework`; `reject`; `comment`; `queryKnobs`; `maxTimeMS` For descriptions of these fields, see [Command Fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-fields) MongoDB doesn't store these settings on the cluster, and they don't apply to other queries with the same [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). To set query settings that persist for a query shape, use [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) MongoDB combines the settings that you pass in the command with any query settings stored on the cluster for the same query shape. If both settings specify the same field, the stored cluster setting takes precedence. **New in version 9.0** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, hint, index, query settings, query shape

- [passage] Unlike the [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash), the [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey) is a function of both the plan cache query shape and the currently available indexes for that shape. Specifically, if indexes that can support the query shape are added or dropped, the `planCacheKey` value may change but the `planCacheShapeHash` value wouldn't change. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, index, plan cache, query shape, explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash, explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md
- [fact] Recommended practice: compare explain('executionStats') (totalDocsExamined, executionTimeMillis) for hinted vs unhinted runs; use a hint to work around a stale cached plan or misleading selectivity, not as a permanent fix without addressing the missing or poorly designed index, since a forced index can worsen as data changes. — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-hint-force-index/view · keywords: executionStats, hint, index, index effectiveness, hint() and Index Forcing
- [passage] | State | Description | | --- | --- | | [Missing](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-missing) | No entry for this shape exists in the cache. For a query, if the cache entry state for a plan cache query shape is [Missing:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-missing) Candidate plans are evaluated and a winning plan is selected.; The cache creates an entry for the plan cache query shape in state [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) with a value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan. | | [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) | The entry in the cache is a placeholder entry for this shape. That is, the planner has seen the shape, calculated a value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan and stored the shape placeholder entry but the plan cache query shape is **not** used to generate query plans. For a query, if the cache entry state for a shape is [Inactive:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) Candidate plans are evaluated and a winning plan is selected.; The selected plan's value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan is compared to the [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry's. If the selected plan's value is:Less than or equal to the [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry's:The selected plan replaces the placeholder [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry and has an [Active](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-active) state.If before the replacement happens, the [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry becomes [Active](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-active) (for example, due to another query operation), the newly active entry will only be replaced if its value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan is greater than the selected plan.; Greater than the [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry's:The [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry remains but its value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan is incremented. | | [Active](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-active) | The entry in the cache is for the winning plan. The planner can use this entry to generate query plans. For a query, if the cache entry state for a shape is [Active:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-active) The active entry is used to generate query plans. The planner also evaluates the entry's performance and if its value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan no longer meets the selection criterion, it will transition to [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) state. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plan-cache-entry-state · keywords: plan cache, query planner, query shape
- [passage] Query knobs are part of the hashed query settings, so they are also part of the [plan cache key](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-plan-cache-key). If you change a knob value, MongoDB produces a new plan cache key, so the planner creates a fresh plan instead of reusing a stale cached plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: plan cache, query planner, query settings
- [passage] Prior to MongoDB 6.0.7, if a [secondary index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-secondary-index) existed on a clustered collection and the secondary index was usable by your query, the query planner selected the secondary index instead of the clustered index by default. In MongoDB 6.1 and prior, to use the clustered index, you must provide a hint because the [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) does not automatically select the clustered index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#behavior · keywords: hint, index, query optimization, query planner

- [passage] For example, the following aggregation operation can be fulfilled by the tree of query plan execution rather than using the aggregation pipeline. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] - Keys Examined (`keysExamined`): Number of index keys scanned for the query. If this metric is `0` for a query that includes filter conditions, it's highly likely there is no index and MongoDB scanned the entire collection. This is a primary cause of slowness. If Docs Examined is very high and Keys Examined is `0` or very low compared to Docs Examined, you're likely scanning the collection or a very unselective index. To learn more, see [Indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, index, keysExamined · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] The second compound index, `{ rated: 1, year: 1 }`, is therefore the more efficient index for supporting the example query, as the MongoDB server only needs to scan `235` [`index keys`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.totalKeysExamined) to find all matching documents using this index, compared to `246` when using the compound index `{ year: 1, rated: 1 }`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, index, { rated: 1, year: 1 }, 235, index keys
- [fact] Fewer documents examined does not guarantee a faster query. Percona's sort example examined fewer documents but ran slower because an extra in-memory SORT stage was needed; Pythian's final index (129 keys vs 82) removed the SORT stage at the cost of a worse key ratio and ran 3 ms vs 2 ms. Check execution time and SORT stages alongside the ratios. — https://www.percona.com/blog/2018/09/06/mongodb-investigate-queries-with-explain-index-usage-part-2/ · keywords: index, index effectiveness, plan stage, Index Effectiveness Measurement
- [passage] | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `unique` | boolean | Optional. Specifies that each index specified in the `keyPatterns` array is a [unique index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique). Unique indexes will not accept insertion or update of documents where the index key value matches an existing value in the index. Specify `true` to create a unique index. The default value is `false`. The option is *unavailable* for [hashed indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md#std-label-index-hashed-index) | | `name` | string | Optional. The name of the index. If unspecified, MongoDB generates an index name by concatenating the names of the indexed fields and the sort order. Options specified to [`db.collection.createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) apply to **all** of the index specifications included in the key pattern array. Since index names must be unique, you may only specify name if you are creating a single index using [`db.collection.createIndexes()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) | | `partialFilterExpression` | document | Optional. If specified, the indexes only reference documents that match the filter expression. See [Partial Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) for more information. A filter expression can include: equality expressions (i.e. `field: value` or using the [`$eq`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#mongodb-query-op.-eq) operator); [`$exists: true`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#mongodb-query-op.-exists) expression; [`$gt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gt.md#mongodb-query-op.-gt), [`$gte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gte.md#mongodb-query-op.-gte), [`$lt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lt.md#mongodb-query-op.-lt), [`$lte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lte.md#mongodb-query-op.-lte) expressions; [`$type`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/type.md#mongodb-query-op.-type) expressions; [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator; [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) operator; [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in) operator; [`$geoWithin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geowithin.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoWithin) operator; [`$geoIntersects`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geointersects.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoIntersects) operator You can specify a `partialFilterExpression` option for all MongoDB [index types.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types) | | `sparse` | boolean | Optional. If `true`, the indexes only reference documents with the specified fields. These indexes use less space but behave differently in some situations (particularly sorts). The default value is `false`. See [Sparse Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) for more information. The following index types are sparse by default and ignore this option: [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index); [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index); [Text](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) For a compound index that includes `2dsphere` index keys and keys for other types, only the `2dsphere` index fields determine whether the index references a document. [Partial indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) have a superset of the sparse index functionality. Unless your application has a specific requirement, use partial indexes instead of sparse indexes. | | `expireAfterSeconds` | integer | Optional. Specifies a value, in seconds, as a time to live ([TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-TTL)) to control how long MongoDB retains documents in this collection. This option only applies to [TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-TTL) indexes. See [Expire Data from Collections by Setting TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-ttl-collections) for more information. If you use TTL indexes created before MongoDB 5.0, or if you want to sync data created in MongDB 5.0 with a pre-5.0 installation, see [Indexes Configured Using NaN](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-expireData-warning) to avoid misconfiguration issues. The TTL index `expireAfterSeconds` value must be within `0` and `2147483647` inclusive. | | [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#std-label-method-createIndexes-hidden) | boolean | Optional. A flag that determines whether the index is [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#std-label-index-type-hidden) from the query planner. A hidden index is not evaluated as part of the query plan selection. Default is `false`. | | `storageEngine` | document | Optional. Allows users to configure the storage engine for the created indexes. The `storageEngine` option should take the following form: `storageEngine: { <storage-engine-name>: <options> }` Storage engine configuration options specified when creating indexes are validated and logged to the [oplog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-oplog) during replication to support replica sets with members that use different storage engines. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#options-for-all-index-types · keywords: index, index bounds, query planner, unique, keyPatterns, true
- [passage] Unlike `planCacheShapeHash`, `planCacheKey` is a function of both the query shape and the currently available indexes for the shape. That is, if indexes that can support the query shape are added/dropped, the `planCacheKey` value may change whereas the `planCacheShapeHash` value would not change. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancachekey · keywords: index, plan cache, query shape, planCacheShapeHash, planCacheKey · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.0, add query settings for query shapes instead of index filters for collections. Index filters are deprecated starting in MongoDB 8.0. Query settings have more functionality than index filters, and index filters aren't persistent after cluster shutdown. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: index, query settings, query shape

- [passage] By hiding an index from the planner, you can evaluate the potential impact of dropping an index without actually dropping the index. If the impact is negative, you can unhide the index instead of having to recreate a dropped index. And because indexes are fully maintained while hidden, the indexes are immediately available for use once unhidden. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.hideIndex/ · keywords: index, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.hideIndex.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/
- [fact] A 1:1 docs-examined to returned ratio does not prove an index is cheap. Pythian's index {certificate_number, address.zip, date} had docs examined equal to returned but over 40k keys examined, and execution time rose 10% versus no index, because the range field came first and the zip filter ran after the fetch. — https://www.pythian.com/blog/choosing-best-index-mongodb-query · keywords: index, index effectiveness, Index Effectiveness Measurement
- [passage] | Chart/Location | Description | | --- | --- | | Connections, Network In, Network Out (Top of panel) | Displays the number of current connections to the machine hosting MongoDB and the number of inbound and outbound bytes as reported by [`mongostat`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongostat) | | CPU, Disk IOPS, and Sys Mem (Top of panel) | Displays the currently used percentage of CPU, disk read and write operations per second, and the total physical memory usage, excluding buffers and swap space, of the machine hosting MongoDB. | | Operations | Displays the number of operations as reported by [`mongostat`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongostat) | | Query Execution Times | Displays latency statistics for current read requests, write requests, and other database commands. Available in MongoDB 3.6 or later. See `opLatencies` at [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/) for more information. On an Atlas Infinite cluster, these metrics describe the compute nodes rather than the storage layer. To learn more, see [MongoDB Atlas Infinite: Architecture.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-architecture.md#std-label-atlas-infinite-architecture) | | Query Targeting | Displays the ratio of documents and objects scanned to documents and objects returned in current queries. These statistics are useful in determining if and how a query uses an index. See [Analyze Query Performance](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/) for more information. The [change streams](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams/) cursors that the MongoDB Search process (`mongot`) uses to keep MongoDB Search indexes updated can contribute to the query targeting ratio and trigger [query targeting alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md#std-label-query-targeting-alerts) if the ratio is high. | | Reads & Writes | Displays the number of active reads, queued reads, active writes, and queued writes as reported by [`mongostat`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongostat) | | Replication Lag | Available only for secondary members of a replica set. Displays the time required to replicate operations from the primary to the secondary members of a replica set. See [Replica Set Secondary Members](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-secondary/) for more information. | | Hottest Collections | Displays the collections with the most operations as reported by [`mongotop`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongotop). For each hot collection, the table also displays the Utilization Percent for the collection. Utilization Percent is calculated from the read and write times as reported by [`mongotop`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongotop) during a sample period. Specifically, the Utilization Percent is the percentage (rounded to the nearest 0.1%) of the read and write times for a collection relative to the read and write times for all collections in the deployment during the sample period. If no read and write operation occur during this period, the Utilization Percent will be 0%. The hottest collections correspond to the most current time displayed in the charts. That is, if the display is running (i.e. not paused), the collections correspond to the hottest collections at the current timestamp. If the display is paused, the collections correspond to the hottest collections at the paused time. If you have [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/) enabled for a collection, the RTPP (Real-Time Performance Panel) doesn't display the collection in this location. Atlas redacts this information. | | Slowest Operations | Displays the slowest operations as reported by [db.currentOp().](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.currentOp/) The operations correspond to the most current time displayed in the charts. That is, if the display is running (i.e. not paused), the operations correspond to the slowest operations at the current timestamp. If the display is paused, the operations correspond to the slowest operations at the paused time. Select one of the operations to open the Operation Details panel, where you can terminate the selected operation using the Kill Op button. The Kill Op button issues the [db.killOp()](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killOp/) method on the selected operation. To use the Kill Op button, you must have [`Project Owner`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Project-Owner), [`Project Data Access Admin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Project-Data-Access-Admin), or [`Project Real Time Performance Operator`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Project-Real-Time-Performance-Operator) access to the project. If you have [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/) enabled for a collection, the RTPP (Real-Time Performance Panel) hides the JSON view of the query if it involves encrypted fields. Atlas redacts this information. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel.md#graph-view · keywords: $currentOp, index, query optimization, mongostat, opLatencies, mongot

- [passage] | Behavior Starting in MongoDB 7.1 | Behavior in Earlier MongoDB Versions | | --- | --- | | Index errors found during the collection scan phase, except duplicate key errors, are returned immediately and then the index build stops. Earlier MongoDB versions return errors in the commit phase, which occurs near the end of the index build. MongoDB 7.1 helps you to rapidly diagnose index errors. For example, if an incompatible index value format is found, the error is returned to you immediately. | Index build errors can take a long time to be returned compared to MongoDB 7.1 because the errors are returned near the end of the index build in the commit phase. | | Increased resilience for your deployment. If an index build error occurs, a [secondary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-secondary) member can request that the [primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary) member stop an index build and the secondary member does not crash. A request to stop an index build is not always possible: if a member has already voted to commit the index, then the secondary cannot request that the index build stop and the secondary crashes (similar to MongoDB 7.0 and earlier). | An index build error can cause a secondary member to crash. | | Improved disk space management for index builds. An index build may be automatically stopped if the available disk space is below the minimum specified in the [`indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB) parameter. If a member has already voted to commit the index, then the index build is not stopped. | An index build is not stopped if there is insufficient available disk space. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#index-builds · keywords: database profiler, index, indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) is idempotent. If you specify an index that does not exist, [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) ignores the non-existent index and completes successfully instead of returning an `IndexNotFound` error. In earlier versions, [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) returns an `IndexNotFound` error if the specified index does not exist. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndex.md#behavior · keywords: $indexStats, index, db.collection.dropIndex(), IndexNotFound · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/dropIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndexes.md
- [fact] The docs state queryShapeHash is derived from the shape itself and is expected to be identical on every node and on replica sets vs sharded clusters in current versions, but advise verifying before reusing it across clusters, versions or after migration. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: query shape, Query Shapes and Query Hash and $queryStats
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, you can use the `queryKnobs` setting to override internal server parameters for a single [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) instead of the whole instance. Set the `queryKnobs` field for targeted queries to mitigate the impact of one regressed shape without changing behavior for other workloads on the same deployment. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: query shape, queryKnobs
- [passage] For example, you can override the [`notablescan`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.notablescan) server parameter for a single query shape instead of the whole instance by setting `queryKnobs` to `{ noTableScan: true }`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: query shape, notablescan, queryKnobs, { noTableScan: true }
- [passage] Unlike [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), which applies per process and can differ between nodes, MongoDB applies the same `queryKnobs` values across the whole cluster for the matching query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: query shape, setParameter, queryKnobs
- [passage] - The Atlas [Query Profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#std-label-query-profiler) records operations that Atlas considers slow when compared to average execution time for all operations on your cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#fix-the-immediate-problem · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] Applications may target different members of a replica set. As such, each replica set member might receive different read commands and have plan cache information that differs from other members. Nevertheless, running `$planCacheStats` on a replica set or a sharded cluster obeys the normal read preference rules. That is, on a replica set, the operation gathers plan cache information from just one member of replica set, and on a sharded cluster, the operation gathers plan cache information from just one member of each shard replica set. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#read-preference · keywords: plan cache, $planCacheStats
- [passage] The Query Profiler differs from the [Database Profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/). The Query Profiler identifies specific inefficient queries based on entries from your `mongod` logs. The Database Profiler returns detailed information about commands executed on the `mongod` based on the specified [profiling level](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/#profiling-levels). Changing the profiling level doesn't impact the slow queries displayed in the Query Profiler. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `resumeAfter` | document | Optional. Directs [`watch()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.watch) to attempt resuming notifications starting after the operation specified in the resume token. Each change stream event document includes a resume token as the `_id` field. Pass the *entire* `_id` field of the change event document that represents the operation you want to resume after. `resumeAfter` is mutually exclusive with `startAfter` and `startAtOperationTime`. | | `startAfter` | document | Optional. Directs [`watch()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.watch) to attempt starting a new change stream after the operation specified in the resume token. Allows notifications to resume after an invalidate event. Each change stream event document includes a resume token as the `_id` field. Pass the *entire* `_id` field of the change event document that represents the operation you want to resume after. `startAfter` is mutually exclusive with `resumeAfter` and `startAtOperationTime`. | | `fullDocument` | string | Optional. By default, [`watch()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.watch) returns the delta of those fields modified by an update operation, instead of the entire updated document. Set `fullDocument` to `"updateLookup"` to direct [`watch()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.watch) to look up the most current majority-committed version of the updated document. [`watch()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.watch) returns a `fullDocument` field with the document lookup in addition to the `updateDescription` delta. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, you can set `fullDocument` to: `"whenAvailable"` to output the document post-image, if available, after the document was inserted, replaced, or updated.; `"required"` to output the document post-image after the document was inserted, replaced, or updated. Raises an error if the post-image is not available. | | `fullDocumentBeforeChange` | string | Optional. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, you can use the new `fullDocumentBeforeChange` field and set it to: `"whenAvailable"` to output the document pre-image, if available, before the document was replaced, updated, or deleted.; `"required"` to output the document pre-image before the document was replaced, updated, or deleted. Raises an error if the pre-image is not available.; `"off"` to suppress the document pre-image. `"off"` is the default. | | `batchSize` | int | Optional. The maximum number of documents that can be returned in each batch of a change stream. By default, [`watch()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.watch) has an initial batch size of the lesser of `101` documents or 16 mebibytes (MiB) worth of documents. Subsequent batches have a maximum size of 16 mebibytes.This option can enforce a smaller limit than 16 MiB, but not a larger one. When set, the `batchSize` is the lesser of `batchSize` documents or 16 MiB worth of documents. Has the same functionality as [`cursor.batchSize()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.batchsize.md#mongodb-method-cursor.batchSize) | | `maxAwaitTimeMS` | int | Optional. The maximum amount of time in milliseconds the server waits for new data changes to report to the change stream cursor before returning an empty batch. Defaults to `1000` milliseconds. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Pass a [collation document](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) to specify a collation for the change stream cursor. Defaults to `simple` binary comparison if omitted. | | `showExpandedEvents` | boolean | Optional. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, change streams support change notifications for DDL events, like the [createIndexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/change-events/createindexes.md#std-label-change-event-createIndexes) and [dropIndexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/change-events/dropindexes.md#std-label-change-event-dropIndexes) events. To include expanded events in a change stream, create the change stream cursor using the `showExpandedEvents` option. **New in version 6.0** | | `startAtOperationTime` | Timestamp | Optional. The starting point for the change stream. If the specified starting point is in the past, it must be in the time range of the oplog. To check the time range of the oplog, see [`rs.printReplicationInfo()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/rs.printreplicationinfo.md#mongodb-method-rs.printReplicationInfo) `startAtOperationTime` is mutually exclusive with `resumeAfter` and `startAfter`. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#fields · keywords: $indexStats, resumeAfter, watch(), _id, startAfter, startAtOperationTime
- [passage] The Atlas Query Profiler records operations that Atlas considers slow when compared to average execution time for all operations on your cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ · keywords: database profiler

## Facts and statements

- [passage] The following example creates an index filter on the `orders` collection such that for queries that consist only of an equality match on the `status` field without any projection and sort, the query optimizer evaluates only the two specified indexes and the collection scan for the winning plan: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#set-filter-on-plan-cache-query-shape-consisting-of-predicate-only · keywords: database profiler, index, plan cache, query optimization, query planner, query settings
- [passage] The [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-optimizer) uses query settings as an additional input during query planning. Index hints in query settings restrict the set of indexes available to the planner, but don't guarantee that the planner will use the index. The planner can still select a collection scan as the winning plan for a given query shape hash. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#definition · keywords: database profiler, hint, index, query optimization, query planner, query settings
- [passage] A boolean that specifies whether MongoDB applied an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) for the [plan cache query shape.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, index, plan cache, query planner, query settings, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Index filters only affect which indexes the planner evaluates; the planner may still select the collection scan as the winning plan for a given plan cache query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: database profiler, index, plan cache, query planner, query settings, query shape
- [fact] executionStats.executionTimeMillis covers plan selection (including the trial phase) plus execution, excludes network transfer, and is not necessarily representative of real query time: with a cached plan or cursor.hint(), plan selection is bypassed and actual time is lower than the reported value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, hint, query planner, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [passage] Increasing the plan cache size adds more cached [plan cache query shapes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) for the [query planner](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization). This can improve query performance, but increases memory usage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#slot-based-execution-parameters · keywords: plan cache, query optimization, query planner, query shape, slot-based execution engine
- [passage] If the query planner selects an index, the explain result includes a `IXSCAN` stage. The stage includes information such as the index key pattern, direction of traversal, and index bounds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#collection-scan · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner, IXSCAN · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [fact] Index hints in query settings (indexHints.allowedIndexes: index name, key pattern or $natural) only restrict the indexes available to the planner; they do not guarantee use, and the planner can still pick a collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md · keywords: database profiler, hint, index, query planner, query settings, Query Settings and Persistent Index Hints (8.0)
- [passage] The following examples create a collection and add query settings for different commands. For all executions of a query shape on the cluster, the examples restrict the query planner to either using the hinted index, or a collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#examples · keywords: database profiler, index, query planner, query settings, query shape
- [passage] Lists the [index filters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) associated with [plan cache query shapes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) for a collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheListFilters.md#definition · keywords: index, plan cache, query planner, query settings, query shape
- [fact] Explain output shape depends on the engine: classic-engine plans put the stage tree at winningPlan.stage with nested inputStage, while slot-based-engine (SBE) plans put it under winningPlan.queryPlan and carry a planNodeId per stage. The docs warn that examples mix both shapes and real output may differ significantly. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: explain plan, plan stage, query planner, slot-based execution engine, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [fact] The three explain('executionStats') counters used to judge an index are nReturned, totalKeysExamined and totalDocsExamined. A COLLSCAN shows totalKeysExamined 0 and totalDocsExamined equal to the collection size (21349 docs scanned to return 3809 in the MongoDB docs example). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, index, index effectiveness, plan stage, Index Effectiveness Measurement
- [passage] - [`queryPlanner.winningPlan.stage`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.winningPlan.stage) displays `COLLSCAN` to indicate a collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: database profiler, explain plan, plan stage, query planner, queryPlanner.winningPlan.stage, COLLSCAN
- [passage] MongoDB runs the [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) to choose the winning plan for the operation under evaluation. [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) returns the [`queryPlanner`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner) information for the evaluated method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#queryplanner-mode · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, query optimization, query planner, cursor.explain(), queryPlanner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/explain.md
- [passage] ```javascript queryPlanner: { winningPlan: { stage: 'SINGLE_SHARD', shards: [ { explainVersion: '1', ... namespace: 'test.pizzaOrders', indexFilterSet: false, parsedQuery: { orderDate: { '$gt': ISODate('2023-01-20T00:00:00.000Z') } }, querySettings: { indexHints: { ns: { db: 'test', coll: 'pizzaOrders' }, allowedIndexes: [ 'orderDate_1' ] }, queryFramework: 'classic', comment: 'Index hint for orderDate_1 index to improve query performance' }, ... } ... ] } } ``` — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#examples · keywords: hint, index, query optimization, query planner, query settings
- [passage] If the query optimizer considered more than one plan, [`executionStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats) information also includes the *partial* execution information captured during the [plan selection phase](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) for both the winning and rejected candidate plans. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#allplansexecution-mode · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, query optimization, query planner
- [passage] planSummary: COLLSCAN keysExamined:0 — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, plan stage, query shape
- [passage] If the `queryPlanner.winningPlan.inputStage.stage` is either `CLUSTERED_IXSCAN` or `IXSCAN`, the index was used. - [passage] The `winningPlan.queryPlan.inputStage.stage` is `DISTINCT_SCAN`, which indicates that the index was used. - [passage] - If you see `"planSummary": "COLLSCAN":` in the query log, the query performed a collection scan and did not use an index. This is a strong signal to add an [index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) or rewrite the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: database profiler, index, plan stage, query shape, "planSummary": "COLLSCAN":
- [fact] If keysExamined is much higher than nreturned, the query scans many index keys; consider adjusting the index. For writes, keysExamined and docsExamined include reads from write-conflict retries, so they can exceed documents matched or modified. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, index, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [passage] Number of documents examined during query execution. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheListFilters.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, query settings, planCacheListFilters, comment, attr.command.cursor.comment · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/killOp.md

- [fact] Profiler level 0 is off, level 1 records operations slower than slowms (or matching a filter), and level 2 records all operations; at level 2 the profiler ignores user-supplied slowms and filter values. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [fact] If a profiling filter is set, slowms and sampleRate no longer apply to the profiler or the diagnostic log. - [fact] MongoDB warns the profiler can degrade performance and disk use, especially at level 2 or with a low slowms at level 1, and points to Atlas Query Profiler / Performance Advisor as alternatives. Blogs advise level 1 with a tuned slowms and a lowered sampleRate on busy systems; avoid level 2 in production. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)

- [passage] Specifies the maximum data size that a collection scan reads. At planning time, MongoDB rejects a query if the query plan requires an unbounded collection scan on a collection whose uncompressed logical data size exceeds this threshold. MongoDB measures the threshold in uncompressed logical bytes, which is equivalent to the `size` field that the [`collStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collstats.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.collStats) command returns, and not the compressed on-disk size. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: database profiler, query planner, size, collStats

- [fact] $indexStats takes an empty document ({ $indexStats: {} }), must be the first stage of an aggregation pipeline, is not allowed in transactions, and with access control requires at least the clusterMonitor role. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats/ · keywords: $indexStats, index, Index Analysis with $indexStats and Unused-Index Detection
- [fact] accesses reports usage only for the node where the query runs, and only user-driven access. TTL-index deletions and chunk split/migration operations do not increment ops. - [fact] Zero ops can be a false negative for unique indexes: a uniqueness check on insert does not increment the ops counter, so an unused-for-reads unique index still enforces a constraint and must not be dropped on stats alone. — https://www.percona.com/blog/identifying-unused-indexes-in-mongodb/ · keywords: $indexStats, index, Index Analysis with $indexStats and Unused-Index Detection

- [passage] If the attempt is unsuccessful, MongoDB applies a set of rules to decide whether the multi-planner should continue or if CBR should evaluate the plans to determine the optimal solution. CBR evaluates each node in a plan based on a cost function and its cardinality estimations. MongoDB selects the plan with the lowest overall cost as the winning plan. Currently, MongoDB only invokes the CBR for a small amount of queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#query-plan-options · keywords: query planner

- [passage] - Hidden indexes are updated upon write operations to the collection and continue to consume disk space and memory. - [fact] Index statistics reset on mongod restart, on index drop and recreation, and on any collMod modification of the index. - [fact] On sharded clusters $indexStats is local to each shard primary and a mongos does not aggregate it; an index can show zero on one shard and serve queries on another, so sum accesses.ops across all shards before calling an index unused (Netdata's guide; MongoDB docs state the per-node scope). — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-unused-indexes/ · keywords: $indexStats, index, Index Analysis with $indexStats and Unused-Index Detection
- [fact] Any DDL event clears the plan cache for the relevant collection (drop collection; create, delete or hide an index). The cache is in memory only and is lost on mongod restart or shutdown. LRU eviction removes the least recently used entry regardless of state. Manual clearing uses getPlanCache().clear() or clearPlansByQuery(). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/query-plans/ · keywords: index, plan cache, Query Planning and Plan Cache

- [fact] Plan cache entries have three states. Missing: no entry exists, so plans are evaluated and an Inactive placeholder with a work value is created. Inactive: placeholder, not used to generate plans. Active: used to generate plans. A newly selected plan whose work value is less than or equal to the placeholder's replaces it and becomes Active. If the value is greater, the placeholder stays and its value is incremented. An Active entry whose work no longer meets the selection criterion drops to Inactive. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/query-plans/ · keywords: plan cache, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [fact] The plan cache is local to each mongod, with no cluster-wide cache. Shards and replica set members can therefore choose different plans for the same shape. — https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-query-plan-cache-explained-performance-pitfalls-and-re-planning/ · keywords: plan cache, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [fact] A query shape groups similar queries by filters, sorts, projections, aggregation pipeline stages and namespace, ignoring literal values; queries with the same specification share one shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: query shape, Query Shapes and Query Hash and $queryStats

- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.0, [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) treats bounds with an equal lower and upper bound as an empty set and does not generate a document with the bound as the field value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#range-bounds-behavior · keywords: index bounds, $densify
- [passage] For example, a [range.bounds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-bounds) of `[10, 10]` generates an extra document with field value `10` in versions prior to 8.0, but does not generate such a document in 8.0 and later. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#range-bounds-behavior · keywords: index bounds, [10, 10], 10

- [passage] Specifies a polygon for a [geospatial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-geospatial) [`$geoWithin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geowithin.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoWithin) query on legacy coordinate pairs. - [passage] The [`$center`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/center.md#mongodb-query-op.-center) operator specifies a circle for a [`$geoWithin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geowithin.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoWithin) query. The query returns legacy coordinate pairs that are within the bounds of the circle. The operator does *not* return GeoJSON objects. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/center.md#definition · keywords: index bounds, $center, $geoWithin
